socialWork.title: Protection Order History Prior to Femicide: Identifying Deaths Involving Granted Court Orders in Washington State
Calculating social work safe staffing caseloads in children’s and older people services in Northern Ireland: A policy development approach
socialWork.abstract: Abstract                   Safe staffing is critical to effective social work practice, workforce sustainability, and staff well-being. Unlike other health and social care professions, social work lacks mandated staffing levels or caseload benchmarks, contributing to workload strain, burnout, and inconsistent service delivery. Using a qualitative narrative approach, expert steering groups from all five Health and Social Care Trusts in Northern Ireland (NI) analysed time allocations for minor, moderate, and complex cases. Weighted analysis (70 percent complex, 20 percent moderate, 10 percent minor) reflected real-world caseload compositions and informed workload modeling across children’s and older people’s services. Indicative safe caseload ranges were identified as 13–15 for Family Intervention Teams, 8–12 for Gateway Teams, 12–18 for Looked After Children Teams, and 30–39 for Older People’s Community Services. Thematic analysis highlighted increasing case complexity, administrative burden, and the importance of supportive communication and supervision. Findings provide an evidence base for emerging Department of Health (NI) policy on safe staffing. Embedding caseload standards, improving data consistency, and reducing bureaucratic pressures are essential to workforce reform. This study advances operationalization of safe staffing levels in social work, strengthening policy, legislation, and sustainable practice.
socialWork.source: The British Journal of Social Work

socialWork.title: Supporting parents with a learning disability in care proceedings: Evidence from the pause programme
socialWork.abstract: Abstract                   Parents with a learning disability are disproportionately represented in the English child protection and family justice systems, with outcomes often shaped by late identification of need, limited reasonable adjustments, and minimal involvement from adult social care. This article draws on one component of a wider study examining the experiences of parents with a learning disability whose children were removed from their care. It presents findings from a mixed-methods study involving professionals working in Pause Practices across England. The analysis identifies five cross-cutting themes: (1) the extent to which Pause was positioned to offer support; (2) delayed identification and diagnosis of learning disability; (3) siloed services and the absence of adult social care involvement; (4) training gaps alongside practitioner adaptation and ingenuity; and (5) ethical dilemmas, particularly in relation to informed consent. Findings indicate that learning disability is frequently identified only once care proceedings are underway, adult social care support is rare even following diagnosis, and reasonable adjustments rely heavily on individual practitioner initiative. The article concludes with recommendations for mandatory professional training, routine early cognitive screening, integrated adult–children’s service protocols, strengthened advocacy, and sustained relationship-based support to prevent avoidable family separations and better align practice with legal obligations.
socialWork.source: The British Journal of Social Work

socialWork.title: Domestic violence and abuse: Thinking and doing differently in child protection
socialWork.abstract: Abstract                   This article explores a mixed methods study, set in two sites in England and one in Scotland, that aimed to understand what constitutes domestic violence and abuse (DVA) in child protection and the relationship with intersecting inequalities. The findings reveal a fragile knowledge base that is impeding the understandings required to comprehend and respond to DVA in differing communities. The lack of contextual information on the socio-economic circumstances of families is a particular gap in light of the finding that, by combining data sets in two of the sites, researchers found a social gradient in operation. This challenges a common framing of DVA as unrelated to poverty and highlights the importance of further research into the links. The international scholarship on intersectionality appears poorly understood. This was reflected in the lack of official data gathered on how pathways for children are impacted by intersecting inequalities. With important exceptions, evidence-based typologies of risk were not used, contributing to ‘one size fits all’ responses to those impacted. The research discusses whether a project constituting individual casework and multi-agency working can carry the weight of expectations being placed upon it by a societal problem such as DVA.
socialWork.source: The British Journal of Social Work

socialWork.title: Antiracist social work in the Nordic countries: A scoping review
socialWork.abstract: Abstract                   Until recently, there has been little acknowledgement of racism as a current phenomenon in Nordic societies, and antiracist social work has been given little attention. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of knowledge on antiracist social work in the Nordic countries and to identify gaps in the literature that can inform further research. A scoping review methodology was employed. Following a systematic search and screening process, supplemented by additional methods to increase recall, we identified 56 publications that met the study’s inclusion criteria. Included publications were categorized based on how racism and discrimination in social work are addressed, resulting in five categories: (1) Discrimination based on race, ethnicity and culture (n = 5), (2) Racism is mentioned, but not explored (n = 9), (3), Racism is addressed, but not within an explicit antiracist social work framework (n = 7), (4) Antiracist social work is addressed and/or applied (n = 10), and (5) Antiracist social work applied as an analytical framework (n = 25). Based on the findings, we see an overall need for more research on racism in social work and for developing methods and strategies for antiracist social work in the Nordic countries, particularly how institutional racism within social work institutions manifests and its consequences.
socialWork.source: The British Journal of Social Work

socialWork.title: Microcredit From Delaying Bill Payments
socialWork.abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Delaying bill payments to public utilities may provide an important strategy for households with volatile incomes to smooth their consumption. At the same time, allowing late payments may reduce net revenues for utilities, which often leads to higher prices to cover costs. Using billing records from a large water utility in Manila, this paper estimates a household consumption and savings model to evaluate counterfactual payment policies. A popular proposal to ensure upfront payments—prepaid metering—recoups less revenue than is needed to compensate households for their loss of consumption smoothing. Alternatively, a revenue‐neutral policy allowing more late payments increases welfare by encouraging greater consumption smoothing.
socialWork.titleZh: 延迟账单支付作为小额信贷
socialWork.abstractZh: 延迟向公共事业公司支付账单可能成为收入波动家庭平滑消费的重要策略。与此同时，允许延迟支付会降低公共事业公司的净收入，从而常常导致价格上涨以弥补成本。本文利用马尼拉一家大型供水公司的账单记录，估计了一个家庭消费与储蓄模型，以评估反事实支付政策。一项确保预付的流行提案——预付费计量——所回收的收入不足以补偿家庭因丧失消费平滑而遭受的损失。相比之下，一种允许更多延迟支付且保持收入中性的政策则通过鼓励更大程度的消费平滑而增加了福利。

socialWork.title: Bad NGOs? Competition in the Market for Donations and Workers' Misconduct
socialWork.abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  In this paper, we investigate how competition among NGOs to attract donations shapes the incentives that NGOs provide to their employees. NGOs hire workers to undertake development projects, which are horizontally and vertically differentiated. Workers perform constructive activities that enhance project quality, but can also engage in non‐observable destructive activities that harm the employing organization. NGOs offer monetary incentives to encourage constructive effort, but also need monitoring to curb destructive behavior. Our analysis yields the following results: (i) a high mission orientation on the part of NGOs makes workers' misconduct harder to eliminate; (ii) increased competition in the market for donations leads to higher constructive effort and project quality, but also to greater destructive effort; (iii) relative to the social optimum, the market outcome entails inadequate monitoring and excessive destructive behavior.
socialWork.titleZh: 坏的非政府组织？捐赠市场竞争与工作人员的不端行为
socialWork.abstractZh: 在本文中，我们研究了非政府组织为吸引捐赠而展开的竞争如何塑造其向员工提供的激励。非政府组织雇佣员工来开展发展项目，这些项目在横向和纵向上存在差异。员工可以从事提高项目质量的积极活动，但也可能从事不可观察的破坏性活动，从而损害所在组织。非政府组织提供金钱激励以鼓励积极努力，但同时也需要监督来遏制破坏性行为。我们的分析得出以下结论：（i）非政府组织高度的使命导向使工作人员的不端行为更难消除；（ii）捐赠市场竞争的加剧会带来更高的积极努力和项目质量，但也会导致更多的破坏性努力；（iii）相对于社会最优水平，市场结果导致监督不足和破坏性行为过度。

socialWork.title: Flexible Contract, Flexible Morale? Microcredit Design and Repayment Discipline
socialWork.abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Flexible repayment benefits borrowers, but practitioners fear increased moral hazard. Investigating their concerns requires disentangling repayment choices from repayment capacity, which is typically infeasible in field studies. We use a lab‐in‐the‐field experiment with 645 microcredit borrowers to cleanly identify the effect of repayment flexibility on moral hazard. We also quantify social pressure. Payoff maximization predicts low repayment in our rigid benchmark contract, and increased repayment with flexibility. Results suggest the opposite: Repayment in the rigid contract is high, and drops substantially under flexible repayment. Social pressure decreases. Our results are consistent with a strong social norm for repayment, which is weakened by introducing flexibility. Norms, which may be inculcated by the lender, may help explain several recent puzzles in microfinance research, including high and equal repayment rates across individual‐ and joint‐liability contracts, and excessive peer pressure. Importantly, norm‐driven behavior may erode with the introduction of flexibility.
socialWork.titleZh: 灵活合约，灵活还款意愿？小额信贷设计与还款纪律
socialWork.abstractZh:
摘要
灵活的还款安排对借款人有益，但从业者担心会加剧道德风险。考察这一担忧需要将还款选择与还款能力分离开来，而实地研究通常难以实现。我们利用一项针对645名小额信贷借款人的实地实验，在受控环境中精确识别还款灵活性对道德风险的影响。我们还量化了社会压力效应。收益最大化理论预测，在刚性基准合约下还款率较低，而在灵活合约下还款率会上升。然而研究结果恰恰相反：刚性合约下的还款率很高，而在灵活还款安排下还款率大幅下降，社会压力也随之减弱。我们的研究结果与一种强有力的还款社会规范相一致，而引入灵活性会削弱这种规范。这种规范可能由贷款机构内化培养，有助于解释小额信贷研究中的若干近期难题，包括个人责任与连带责任合约下均出现的高且相近的还款率，以及过度的同伴压力。重要的是，由规范驱动的行为可能因引入灵活性而逐渐消退。

socialWork.title: To Grandmother's House We Go: Informal Childcare and Female Labor Mobility
socialWork.abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  We document how childcare costs and the location of extended family influence the labor supply and mobility of US women. Women return to their home locations immediately before fertility events, suggesting that informal childcare needs may motivate home migration. Women who live near their parents have lower child earnings penalties. We then build a model of labor supply and migration to assess the impacts of childcare subsidies. Childcare subsidies increase earnings and mobility among US women and ignoring migration can understate the welfare benefits of these policies, especially for college‐educated women and those whose parents' locations have poor amenities.
socialWork.titleZh: 去外婆家：我们考察非正式儿童照护与女性劳动力流动
socialWork.abstractZh: 摘要：我们记录了儿童照护成本与大家庭所在地如何影响美国女性的劳动力供给与流动。研究显示，女性会在生育事件发生前立即返回家乡，表明非正式儿童照护需求可能是其返乡迁移的动因。居住在父母附近的女性所面临的子女收入惩罚更低。随后我们构建了一个劳动力供给与迁移模型，以评估儿童照护补贴政策的影响。研究发现，儿童照护补贴能够提高美国女性的收入水平和流动能力；忽略迁移因素会低估此类政策带来的福利收益，对受过大学教育的女性以及那些父母所在地区公共设施较差的女性而言尤其如此。
